**Version history (from the Universe page)**

- **Latest: 2.0.0** (October 14, 2026) — minimum Typst version **0.15.0**.
- Prior releases: 1.3.0 (Mar 28, 2025), 1.2.0 (Jan 7, 2025), 1.1.1 (Dec 4, 2024), 1.1.0 (Dec 2, 2024), 1.0.0 (Jul 17, 2024), 0.2.1, 0.2.0, 0.1.0 (Nov 6, 2023).
- **Typst 0.14:** The page doesn't list minimum compiler versions for older releases, so it can't be confirmed from this content alone. Since 2.0.0 is the only release requiring 0.15, the best candidate is **1.3.0**, the most recent pre-2.0 version — but you'd need to check its own package page to verify.

**Features (2.0.0)**

- **Line numbers:** Enabled with a single show rule (`#show raw.where(block: true): codly.new`); numbering format is configurable, wrapped rows keep their source number, and custom gutter columns can be added or all gutters hidden.
- **Highlighting with labels/annotations:** Span highlights on character ranges can carry tags and labels; brace annotations mark line ranges; callouts can track indentation or point at a character. References are native: "use `@block:5` for a line and `@highlight` for a labeled span." Positions are one-based and inclusive, counting indentation.
- **Skipping lines:** `range` selects one interval, `ranges` several; "Disjoint excerpts preserve their gaps." `offset` can renumber from one or continue from another block's label.
- **Zebra striping:** `codly.line-set_(fill: ...)` takes a single paint, "a cycling array of paints," or a per-row callback — the cycling array gives alternating row colors.
- **Language icons/names:** Provided through the companion `codly-languages` package via `codly.lang-set_(languages: codly-languages)`; a filename badge is also supported.

Also included: six themes (default `thesis`), syntax-aware diffs (`diff-py`), figure/listing integration, and optional indent guides, rainbow delimiters, and wrap markers.

content.content:
**arkheion** is a Typst template by Manuel Goulão that recreates the look of the LaTeX layouts commonly seen on arXiv and bioRxiv, drawing on the `arxiv-style` project. The page describes it as "A simple template reproducing popular arXiv templates."

Imported with `#import "@preview/arkheion:0.1.2": arkheion, arkheion-appendices`, the template is applied via a show rule (`arkheion.with(...)`) that accepts the paper's front-matter: a `title` string, an `authors` list where each entry can carry a name, email, affiliation, and ORCID, an `abstract` given as content, a `keywords` list of strings, and a `date` string. There is also a `custom-authors` parameter for supplying your own author block in place of the generated one—though the `authors` list must still be provided (names only are sufficient) so the document metadata can be produced. A second function, `arkheion-appendices`, switches the remainder of the document into appendix styling.

The current release is **0.1.2**, published April 7, 2026, following 0.1.1 (October 1, 2025) and the initial 0.1.0 release (March 23, 2024). It is MIT-licensed, weighs in at about 5 kB, and is filed under the Paper category for Engineering and Computer Science. The source lives at github.com/mgoulao/arkheion, which is also where issues should be reported.

Regarding a minimum Typst version: the page does not state one, so I can't confirm a compiler requirement from this content alone. (The codly notes appearing alongside your query concern a different package and don't apply to arkheion.)

content.content:
**Yes.** The 0.14.0 changelog (October 24, 2025) lists it under both Highlights and Model:

> "Added `title` element for displaying the document title" (PR #5618)

**Other relevant additions in this release**

*Document front matter*
- The `document` function's `authors` and `keywords` properties now produce HTML `<meta>` tags.
- PDF heading bookmarks now include the heading's numbering.
- `title` is also among the elements that are newly locatable via `query`/`locate` without a label.

*Raw code blocks*
- HTML export: `raw` gains syntax highlighting; block-level `raw` now emits both `<code>` and `<pre>`; the language is kept as a `data-lang` attribute on `<code>`.
- Default highlighting theme was tweaked for more accessible colors; JSON keys and string values now get distinct colors.
- Fixes: crash on a custom syntax with an unescaped trailing backslash; tab indentation with CRLF line endings; equality checks between `raw.line` elements.
- `raw` is now locatable without a label.

*Layout*
- Opt-in character-level justification via the new `par.justification-limits` property, described as able to "significantly improve the appearance of justified text".
- Tables: support for multiple headers and subheaders; headers now force a row break; fixed headers/footers absorbing non-header cells.
- Fixed a breakable block producing an empty segment when nothing fit in the first segment (affected fills, strokes, stickiness).
- Fixed a crash from set rules for colspan/rowspan on grid cells; fixed CJK-Latin spacing at manual line breaks and sub/superscript boundaries; fixed wrong line-break opportunities around object replacement characters.
- Improved spacing of nested tight lists; fixed hanging indent for centered, numbered headings.
- Math-adjacent: new `frac.style` for skewed/inline fractions; `vec`/`cases` layout made consistent with `mat`.

Note: the appended "proactive context" material about the codly package is not part of the Typst changelog page and wasn't used for this answer.

**How to apply:** Before proposing a Typst package for Twyne, check its `compiler` field in `https://packages.typst.org/preview/index.json`, and plan either to vendor the package through `mapShadow` or to add a package registry to the worker. See [[twyne-genre-kits-research]].

content.text:
The idea holds up well against both the codebase and Typst Universe. Here is what I found and how I'd shape it.

**Two facts constrain the design.** Twyne's bundled compiler is Typst 0.14.x, confirmed by version strings inside the WASM. That is new enough for the native `title` element, which the Typst docs say should appear once per document, with level 1 headings reserved for sections. The compiler has no package registry wired in, so no Universe package works today. The worker can shadow files into the virtual filesystem, so vendoring a package is already possible without a network fetch.

**Proposed shape: a "kit" per piece type.** A kit is a bundle of four things that travel together:

- **Roles** the writer can apply. Subtitle, kicker, standfirst, epigraph, scene break are shared. Kits add their own: abstract and affiliations for a paper, character cue and stage direction for a play, callout and annotated code for a technical post.
- **A Typst theme layer** of set and show rules for those roles, appended after the existing editorial styles in `src/utils/typst/theme.ts`.
- **Slash and toolbar entries** registered through the existing command registry, which already supports grouped slash menus. Kit roles would appear in a new "Piece" group.
- **Vendored packages** mapped into the worker through the existing shadow mechanism, only when the kit needs them.

The document would carry a `kit` field alongside `format` and `typstSource`, defaulting to the current essay look so nothing existing changes.

**Where each kit would draw from Typst Universe.** All versions and compiler floors below come from the live package index.

| Kit | Package | Version | Needs Typst | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Technical blog | zebraw | 0.6.3 | 0.14 | Line numbers and line highlighting, lightweight. Works today. |
| Technical blog | codly | 2.0.0 | 0.15 | Richer: ranged highlights with labels, brace annotations, skips, diffs. Blocked until compiler upgrade. codly 1.3.0 is the last pre-0.15 release. |
| Report | fletcher plus cetz | 0.5.8 / 0.5.2 | 0.13 / 0.14 | Flowcharts, state machines, node-and-arrow diagrams. |
| Report | cetz-plot or lilaq | 0.1.4 / 0.6.0 | 0.13 | Charts from data. |
| Report | gentle-clues or showybox | 1.3.1 / 2.0.4 | 0.13 / 0.12 | Admonitions and callout boxes. |
| Academic paper | arkheion | 0.1.2 | unstated | arXiv-style title block, authors with affiliations and ORCID, abstract, keywords. No two-column option, but Twyne already has a columns setting. |
| Academic paper | charged-ieee | 0.1.4 | 0.12 | IEEE two-column alternative. |
| Academic paper | theorion | 0.6.0 | 0.13 | Theorem and proof environments. |
| Play | stagehand | 0.1.0 | 0.13 | Stageplays. |
| Play | playwright | 0.1.0 | unstated | Dramatists Guild formatting. |
| Screenplay | screen-scripted | 0.1.0 | 0.14.2 | Automatic dialogue continuation across pages. |
| Screenplay | celluloid | 0.1.0 | unstated | AMPAS guidelines. |
| Poetry | verseatile | 0.2.2 | unstated | Verse layout. |
| Fiction or book | tieffiction, wonderous-book, folklore | various | 0.13 or unstated | Running headers, chapter openers, author commentary. |
| Any | marginalia | 0.3.1 | 0.12 | Sidenotes and margin figures. |

**The technical blog kit deserves the most editor work.** Typst's native `raw` already does syntax highlighting when given a language, but the serializer at `src/utils/typst/serialize.ts:212` drops the language, so exported code blocks are unhighlighted today. That is a quick win independent of any kit. On top of it, the kit would add a line-highlight attribute on the code block node, a per-line annotation that renders as a callout, and a "breakdown" mode that splits one snippet into numbered excerpts with prose between them. zebraw covers highlight and numbering now. codly's labelled highlights and brace annotations are the better long-term target, which argues for upgrading typst.ts when a 0.15 build ships.

**Editing experience matters more than packages.** Today any Typst Twyne does not recognise becomes an opaque block in Write view. Each kit role needs a Tiptap node with its own rendering in the editor, a serializer case, and a parse case in the source bridge, or it is source-only. I would scope the first slice to the shared roles plus one kit, and treat packages as rendering detail behind a role rather than as the feature itself.

**Recommended order.**

1. Add `lang` to code block export and the native `title` element for the document title. Both are small and unblock the rest.
2. Shared roles: subtitle, kicker, standfirst, epigraph, scene break, with theme rules and slash entries.
3. Kit selection in document settings, stored on the document, defaulting to the current essay look.
4. Technical blog kit with zebraw vendored through the worker's shadow filesystem.
5. Academic paper kit next, since abstract, affiliations, and columns are mostly front-matter roles and Twyne already has columns.
6. Play and screenplay kits once the role model has proven itself, because they change paragraph semantics most.

This was research only. Nothing in the repository changed. I saved a memory noting the compiler version and the missing package registry so future package proposals get checked against it first.

input.title: Twyne: editorial roles, kits, and Typst export fixes
input.task:
Repository: /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne (Tiptap editor + Typst export, Convex backend). Read CLAUDE.md and convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md before touching anything under convex/. Work on a new branch `feat/editorial-roles-and-kits` off main. Commit in logical steps (do not push). Do not run the full test suite or repeated full `tsc` runs; use targeted vitest files and a single `npx tsc --noEmit` at the end.

## Background (already researched, do not redo)

- Twyne's bundled Typst compiler (`@myriaddreamin/typst.ts` 0.7.0) is Typst 0.14.x. The native `title` element exists. There is NO package registry wired into `src/utils/typst/compiler.worker.ts`; only `compiler.addSource("/main.typ", …)` and `compiler.mapShadow(path, bytes)` are used. `#import "@preview/…"` will fail. Vendoring a package means shadowing its files into the virtual FS.
- Editorial Typst styles live in `src/utils/typst/theme.ts` (`TYPST_EDITORIAL_STYLES`). HTML→Typst serialization is `src/utils/typst/serialize.ts`. The Typst source ↔ HTML bridge is `src/utils/typst/document.ts`. Unknown Typst becomes an opaque `rawTypst` node (`src/components/editor/extensions/raw-typst.ts`).
- The command registry is `src/utils/editor-commands.ts`; slash menu groups are "Structure", "Write", "Insert", "Review". `/subtitle` currently just aliases Heading 2 (`paragraph.heading-2` searchTerms/keywords).
- Layout types (columns 1|2|3, columnGap) are in `src/types/index.ts`. Document persistence fields `format` and `typstSource` exist in `src/utils/idb.ts`, `src/utils/convex-sync.ts`, `convex/schema.ts`, `convex/sync.ts`.
- Serializer bug: `src/utils/typst/serialize.ts` around line 212 emits `#raw(text)` for `<pre>` and drops the language, so exported code blocks are never syntax highlighted.

## Deliverables, in order. Finish each before the next.

### 1. Quick wins
a. Code block language in export: carry Tiptap's codeBlock `language` attribute (check how it renders to HTML, typically `<pre><code class="language-xyz">`) through to `#raw(…, lang: "xyz", block: true)`. Keep the no-language path unchanged. Make sure the Typst-source→HTML bridge in document.ts round-trips the lang back onto the code block if it parses raw blocks at all.
b. Document title: where serialize.ts emits the document title as `#heading(level: 1)[…]` (see the export payload path near the bottom of serialize.ts), switch to `#title[…]` plus `#set document(title: …)`. Add a `#show title:` rule in theme.ts that reproduces the current level‑1 title look (size 30pt, Libre Baskerville, tracking, spacing). Confirm the compile still works by running whatever existing Typst compile/export test exists (grep for tests referencing `serialize` or `export`), or by a small vitest that serializes a fixture and asserts the `#title` output. Level 1 headings remain available for sections.

### 2. Shared editorial roles (Tiptap nodes + Typst)
Add block nodes in `src/components/editor/extensions/editorial-roles.ts` (one file, one Tiptap Node each): `subtitle`, `kicker`, `standfirst`, `epigraph` (with optional `attribution` child or attribute), `sceneBreak` (atom, attribute `style: "ornament" | "rule" | "space"`). Each must:
- Render in the editor with its own class (`twyne-role-subtitle` etc.) and sensible default CSS in the editor stylesheet (find where `.twyne-raw-typst` or heading styles are defined and add next to them). Keep it tasteful and consistent with the existing editorial look.
- parseHTML/renderHTML with `data-role="…"` so HTML persistence and sync are unaffected.

Work on a new branch `feat/editorial-roles-and-kits` off main. Commit in logical steps (do not push). Do not run the full test suite or repeated full `tsc` runs; use targeted vitest files and a single `npx tsc --noEmit` at the end.

## Background (already researched, do not redo)

- Twyne's bundled Typst compiler (`@myriaddreamin/typst.ts` 0.7.0) is Typst 0.14.x. The native `title` element exists. There is NO package registry wired into `src/utils/typst/compiler.worker.ts`; only `compiler.addSource("/main.typ", …)` and `compiler.mapShadow(path, bytes)` are used. `#import "@preview/…"` will fail. Vendoring a package means shadowing its files into the virtual FS.
- Editorial Typst styles live in `src/utils/typst/theme.ts` (`TYPST_EDITORIAL_STYLES`). HTML→Typst serialization is `src/utils/typst/serialize.ts`. The Typst source ↔ HTML bridge is `src/utils/typst/document.ts`. Unknown Typst becomes an opaque `rawTypst` node (`src/components/editor/extensions/raw-typst.ts`).
- The command registry is `src/utils/editor-commands.ts`; slash menu groups are "Structure", "Write", "Insert", "Review". `/subtitle` currently just aliases Heading 2 (`paragraph.heading-2` searchTerms/keywords).
- Layout types (columns 1|2|3, columnGap) are in `src/types/index.ts`. Document persistence fields `format` and `typstSource` exist in `src/utils/idb.ts`, `src/utils/convex-sync.ts`, `convex/schema.ts`, `convex/sync.ts`.
- Serializer bug: `src/utils/typst/serialize.ts` around line 212 emits `#raw(text)` for `<pre>` and drops the language, so exported code blocks are never syntax highlighted.

## Deliverables, in order. Finish each before the next.

### 1. Quick wins
a. Code block language in export: carry Tiptap's codeBlock `language` attribute (check how it renders to HTML, typically `<pre><code class="language-xyz">`) through to `#raw(…, lang: "xyz", block: true)`. Keep the no-language path unchanged. Make sure the Typst-source→HTML bridge in document.ts round-trips the lang back onto the code block if it parses raw blocks at all.
b. Document title: where serialize.ts emits the document title as `#heading(level: 1)[…]` (see the export payload path near the bottom of serialize.ts), switch to `#title[…]` plus `#set document(title: …)`. Add a `#show title:` rule in theme.ts that reproduces the current level‑1 title look (size 30pt, Libre Baskerville, tracking, spacing). Confirm the compile still works by running whatever existing Typst compile/export test exists (grep for tests referencing `serialize` or `export`), or by a small vitest that serializes a fixture and asserts the `#title` output. Level 1 headings remain available for sections.

### 2. Shared editorial roles (Tiptap nodes + Typst)
Add block nodes in `src/components/editor/extensions/editorial-roles.ts` (one file, one Tiptap Node each): `subtitle`, `kicker`, `standfirst`, `epigraph` (with optional `attribution` child or attribute), `sceneBreak` (atom, attribute `style: "ornament" | "rule" | "space"`). Each must:
- Render in the editor with its own class (`twyne-role-subtitle` etc.) and sensible default CSS in the editor stylesheet (find where `.twyne-raw-typst` or heading styles are defined and add next to them). Keep it tasteful and consistent with the existing editorial look.
- parseHTML/renderHTML with `data-role="…"` so HTML persistence and sync are unaffected.
- Serialize to Typst in serialize.ts as named functions defined in theme.ts: `#twyne-subtitle[…]`, `#twyne-kicker[…]`, `#twyne-standfirst[…]`, `#twyne-epigraph(attribution: […])[…]`, `#twyne-scene-break(style: "ornament")`. Define those functions in `TYPST_EDITORIAL_STYLES` with typography in keeping with the existing rules (DM Sans small caps for kicker, larger Lora for standfirst, italic indented epigraph with right-aligned attribution, centered ornament/rule/space for scene break).
- Round-trip from Typst source back to the HTML nodes in document.ts, following how existing constructs (e.g. heading, quote, footnote) are recognised there. If a role cannot be recognised it must at least fall back to rawTypst without crashing.
- Register commands in editor-commands.ts under a new slash group "Piece" (ids `role.subtitle`, `role.kicker`, `role.standfirst`, `role.epigraph`, `role.scene-break`). Remove "subtitle" from the Heading 2 searchTerms/keywords. Wire the commands wherever the other paragraph commands are executed (grep for `paragraph.heading-2` to find the dispatcher in twyne-editor.tsx / slash-command.ts).
- Add a vitest file `editorial-roles.test.ts` next to the extension covering: insert each role via command, HTML round-trip, Typst serialization string for each.

### 3. Kit selection
- Add `kit?: "essay" | "technical" | "paper" | "play"` to the document type (find where `format`/`typstSource` live in the document type and add alongside; default/undefined means "essay", which must produce byte-identical Typst to today except for the title and lang changes from step 1). Persist it through idb, convex-sync, convex/schema.ts (optional field, use `v.optional(v.union(v.literal(...)))`), and convex/sync.ts the same way `format` is handled.
- Create `src/utils/typst/kits.ts` exporting a `KITS` record: `{ id, label, description, roles: string[] (command ids enabled), typstStyles: string (appended after TYPST_EDITORIAL_STYLES), vendoredPackages: {path, url}[] (empty for now) }`. Essay kit = empty extras. content.text:
Sonnet 5.5 finished all four steps. The work sits on the branch `feat/editorial-roles-and-kits` as four commits, not pushed, no PR. I verified it independently after its final commit.

**Verification results**

- Targeted tests pass: the serializer suite, the new editorial-roles and code-block-lines suites, slash commands, formatting, and editor commands. The serializer tests compile every role, all four kits, and highlighted code through the real bundled Typst compiler with no diagnostics.
- One full type check is clean.
- One failure in `convex-sync.test.ts` is pre-existing. I reproduced the identical Qwik `__EXPERIMENTAL__ is not defined` error on a clean checkout of main, so it is unrelated to this branch.

**What landed**

1. **Export fixes.** Code blocks now carry their language into Typst `raw`, so exports get syntax highlighting. The document title uses the native `title` element with a show rule that reproduces the old look.
2. **Editorial roles.** Eight Tiptap nodes: subtitle, kicker, standfirst, epigraph with attribution, scene break with ornament, rule, or space styles, abstract, character cue, and stage direction. Each has editor CSS, a Typst function in the theme, serialization, round-trip from Typst source, and a slash command in a new "Piece" group. Heading 2 no longer claims the subtitle alias.
3. **Kits.** A `kit` field persisted through IndexedDB, sync, and the Convex schema. The essay kit is the default and a test asserts it exports identically to no kit. Technical, paper, and play kits append their own Typst styles and gate which Piece commands appear. A "Piece type" select lives in the Page layout panel.
4. **Line highlighting.** A `highlightLines` attribute on code blocks, a slash command that prompts for ranges, a Typst function that renders numbered lines with highlighted fills, and matching editor CSS. Applies only in the technical kit.

**Things to know before merging**

- Sonnet found that real exports mostly flow through the native Typst source path rather than the HTML serializer, so it wired role and code handling into both paths.
- The paper kit does not set smaller margins. The page setup emits its own `#set page` after kit styles and would override it, so margins would have to come through layout settings.
- Nothing was driven in a real browser. The Piece type select, slash filtering, and highlight prompt are covered by unit tests and type checks only.
- The working tree holds unrelated uncommitted edits to scene-bench, pricing, settings, and `src/types/index.ts`, plus new untracked scene-media files. They were present before Sonnet started and were kept out of every commit. The tree was clean when this thread began, so another session appears to be working in the same checkout.

Suggested next step is a browser pass over the four UI touchpoints, then a PR.
